claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 12065 - National Security Information (28 June 1978)
claims.text: It is EO 12065, and not EO 12356, that revoked EO 11652: section 6-203 does so. The chain runs 10501 to 11652 to 12065 to 12356, and skipping 12065 is the most common way to get it wrong.

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 12065 - National Security Information (28 June 1978)
claims.text: THE BALANCING TEST, IN THE ORDER'S OWN WORDS. Section 3-303 required an official to 'determine whether the public interest in disclosure outweighs the damage to national security'. No classification order since has carried it.

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 12356 - National Security Information (2 April 1982)
claims.sourceText: EO 12356 full text term searches, against EO 12065 sec. 3-303, https://www.archives.gov/federal-register/codification/executive-order/12356.html and https://irp.fas.org/offdocs/eo/eo-12065.htm
claims.text: THE PUBLIC-INTEREST TEST IS GONE, AND THIS WAS CHECKED FROM BOTH SIDES. The phrase 'public interest' occurs zero times in EO 12356, as does any form of 'balanc'. Its predecessor EO 12065 had required at section 3-303 that an official 'determine whether the public interest in disclosure outweighs the damage to national security'. The obligation to weigh disclosure against harm was removed in 1982 and has not returned.

edges.label: Revokes it, and with it the public-interest balancing test
edges.note: Section 6.2(d): 'Executive Order No. 12065 of June 28, 1978, as amended, is revoked as of the effective date of this Order.' EO 12065 sec. 3-303 had required an official to determine whether the public interest in disclosure outweighed the damage to national security. The phrase 'public interest' occurs zero times in EO 12356.
